rules.statement: A lease is void as against a subsequent mortgagee who registered his mortgage prior to the lease, even if the registration of the mortgage and the lease are in different books.
rules.supporting_quote: "To escape from this situation Mr. Drieberg for the defendants, appellants, addressed three arguments to us. He argued that as the decree was obtained upon four bonds, and one of them was unconnected with the land in dispute and other lands than the one in dispute were also sold under the same decree, that it was not clear that the sale to the plaintiff was under the mortgage created by the bond subsequent in date to the lease. This argument is not sound. The decree was for a lump sum which included the sum due on that bond. Accordingly, the sale of the share in dispute under the decree must be deemed to have been upon the mortgage created by that bond."
